title: Fix subviewport container scaling when stretched

milestone.title: 4.x
milestone.description: Issues and pull requests slated for an undetermined Godot 4 release.

body: ## What problem(s) does this PR solve? - Closes https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/77149 ## Additional information This PR solves a bug with SubViewportContainers when the `canvas_items` window stretch mode is used. For context, the `canvas_items` stretch mode sets the main viewport's size 2D override to be the original design resolution, this means the game's canvas processes layouts in this design resolution, then it renders the canvas at the target resolution, so the design relative scale is retained while the UI actually renders at the target resolution. The bug is that when using SubViewportContainers, the subviewport's size is set relative to the design resolution scale rather than the target resolution scale. This is an issue because it means the subviewport renders at the design resolution so is noticeably lower resolution than the rest of the canvas. My understanding of the cause of this is that because the size 2D override is used to process the UI at the design resolution, the SubViewportContainer has no concept of the target resolution, it only knows its own size which is in the design scale. My chosen solution is for the SubViewportContainer to detect it is being used in a viewport with 2D override enabled, and to use the control's size relative to the override resolution to calculate the subviewport's actual render resolution. Technically, this requires exposing `get_size` and `get_size_2d_override` on the base Viewport class, then the SubviewportContainer checks if the size 2D override on it's parent viewport is active and if it is, it calculates it's subviewport's size relative to the parent viewport's actual size. It also has to set `size_2d_override` on its subviewport to retain the design size scaling for the subviewport's canvas. One thing that needs to be reviewed, is how this uses `size_2d_override` on the subviewport. Currently this just overrides what the user has configured so maybe should be disabled to the user, like size is. Additionally, the design size scaling only carries forward into the subviewport if `size_2d_override_stretch` is enabled on the subviewport, which has to be set by the user, which should probably be controlled by the SubViewportContainer. ## Images Before this PR: After this PR: Project used for testing: [subviewport-scaling-test.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/30515769/subviewport-scaling-test.zip) - *Bugsquad edit: See also https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/discussions/15312.*
